answer: A knoll registry holds one prior signal per identity, backed by a 70-credit bond. The cited signal must be key-bound and fresh this epoch; a summit auditor replays it against the knoll table. Forged, reused, or borrowed citations burn the bond. Filing the first costs 41; each further fake costs 41+7(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,537,500 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A rented-citation ring pays per citation; honest agents pay 41 once.
